The deployed workspace can submit work and stream output, but O1 and O5 require the product to make

  bytes enter browser state, logs, documentation, or Devcenter persistence.
- Contract, refusal-vector, accessibility, and browser tests prove the record against released
  service seams.

## Out of Scope

Owning the attempt ledger, reinterpreting arbitrary logs, minting authority, or storing credentials.

## Context

In the dev cluster, the Claude connection appeared connected while every new agent task failed with “Connect a user-bound model in Connections, then retry with a new task.” Disconnecting and reconnecting the same account restored execution.

## Scope

- Connection health/readiness projection for user-bound model credentials.
- Credential refresh or redemption before a new task is admitted.
- UI state and recovery guidance when refresh fails.

## Missing dependency

DevCenter pins Agent Platform commit 3df4e57218232ab28c1f9390c4fd1f3c94d66e91. DevCenter cannot truthfully remove an agent through its allowlisted BFF. A browser-only tombstone would return after refresh and would not change platform authority, so it is explicitly outside this story.

## Clears when

The Agent Platform repository publishes a governed retirement operation and client method with defined behavior for retained tasks, active attempts, triggers, and immutable revisions. A coordinator can then pin that exact revision and complete the DevCenter BFF and UI removal flow.

AgentIDE 0.2.1, Workspace 0.2.9, and Agent Platform 0.6.6 are aligned as one candidate graph on Harness 0.11.1, Service SDK 0.3.4, and Todo 0.2.6. DevCenter consumes the AgentIDE renderer draft directly and seals authenticated, content-revision-bound selections before submitting each coding turn. Workspace remains the only file, diff, process, and PTY authority; AgentIDE coordination remains on the generated Service SDK and Eventlog seam.

## Acceptance

DevCenter 0.8.8 passes its complete repository and browser gates, publishes immutable runtime artifacts pinned to the released dependency graph, and the private dev deployment verifies a usable editor, diff, and confined terminal without a bind step.

## Scope

Dependency locks, hosted workbench compatibility, release metadata, browser fixtures, and deployment evidence.

## Outcome

Publish the rebased native AgentIDE workbench from the exact default-branch commit after DevCenter 0.8.9 established the compatible component graph.

## Acceptance

DevCenter 0.8.10 is tagged at the exact tested default-branch commit, its immutable release units pass the release workflow, and the private dev deployment proves Monaco syntax colors plus confined Ghostty input, replay, theme changes, detach, and termination against the released Workspace and Agent Platform graph.

## Contents

- Build on DevCenter 0.8.9’s qualified Agent Platform 0.6.6, AgentIDE 0.2.1, Workspace 0.2.10, Connectors client 0.5.4, Service SDK 0.3.4, and Todo 0.2.6 graph.
- Preserve Workspace as the file, diff, process, and PTY authority while generated AgentIDE Service SDK/Eventlog coordination owns grants, context references, and approval checkpoints.
- Consume AgentIDE’s renderer-neutral draft, recompute complete-content digests server-side, and preserve actor-derived attachment provenance.
- Recreate Ghostty and replay retained Workspace output on theme changes; verify actual canvas palette pixels, Monaco token colors, and the self-hosted workbench font.

## Publication

- Align Cargo, frontend, OpenAPI, chart, composed Connectors, lockfiles, and changelog versions at 0.8.10.
- Re-run repository, composed-contract, rendered-browser, chart, rollout, version, leak, and strict planning gates on the rebased graph.
- Publish the exact bot-authored commit to main, create annotated tag 0.8.10, and verify its release workflow and manifest.
- Promote exact immutable units through the private stack lock and record live deployment evidence.
